claims: NASA successfully launched the Artemis II mission on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II mission sent four astronauts on a 10-day, 695,000-mile journey around the Moon.
The crew of the Artemis II mission consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The launch vehicle for the Artemis II mission is the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The spacecraft for the Artemis II mission is the Orion capsule named Integrity.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight test of the SLS and Orion systems.
Artemis II travels further from Earth than any human since Apollo 17 in 1972.
The crew of Artemis II will perform systems tests, including life support checks, to prepare for future lunar surface missions Artemis III and IV.
Christina Koch is the first woman on a lunar mission.
Victor Glover is the first person of color on a lunar mission.
Jeremy Hansen is the first non-U.S. citizen on a lunar mission.
The crew of Artemis II is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean after completing their lunar flyby.
